controls: Removing the single added workflow step restores the entire old workflow byte-for-byte: all actions, 12 matrix cells, job dependencies, mandatory commands, 30-minute limit, source security gate and artifact rules remain intact. Existing test ASTs, real adapters, workload, assertions, deadlines and coverage definitions are unchanged.
method: Assisted contextual review by /root and separate deterministic verification; no independent human audit claimed.
new_tests: Three tests examine ordering and budget, execute the actual PowerShell through the unchanged strict ShellRunner, preserve earlier exports, and refuse missing/relative/empty/line-break/junction inputs before export writes. The old workflow and two unsafe variants are retained as observed refusals.
new_workflow_boundary: Only the Windows quality job changes its temporary-file location. The fixed names TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP receive the runner-owned allocated directory through GITHUB_ENV. Null/empty, CR/LF, relative, absent and reparse final paths refuse before writing. Values are passed as PowerShell variables, never parsed as command source. Existing environment-file content is preserved; a write failure remains fatal.
performance: Three alternating 1000-row microbenchmark pairs favor the allocated volume with DELETE/FULL and all integrity checks unchanged. One full pair on one native Windows/Python 3.12 VM runs the unchanged 50000-host test twice: 770.3269527 versus 57.3042041 seconds. Both succeed under 96 MiB Python allocation peak; order/cache effects are not excluded. No SSH hardware or universal latency claim.
qualification_limit: C155 PR success does not mask its cancelled push. C157 must receive exact-source operator approval then pass the full native CI before any merge or D publication.
rejected_optimization: No production journal/locking change: local wall-time pairs were mixed and native exclusive locking regressed P99. These unfavorable observations remain in c156-native-experiments.json.
security_assessments: Unchanged warning sites retain their reviewed trust boundaries, parameterized SQL, fixed argv, safe fixture literals and bounded owners. The new tests call the already reviewed strict QA shell with owned scripts; no arbitrary inventory code or credentials are introduced. Python Bandit does not analyze the embedded PowerShell, which is separately inspected and exercised by the positive and negative contracts.
signals: All 181 raw signals are byte-identical to C155, with identical source AST and named scope. No warning is located in a changed file; this mapping grants no approval.
